main_text.p: qua certitudo quantum expedit rebus humanis ; cum sit jurisjurandi religio {b}expediendarum litium maximum reme-dium. Ast æquivocatione tollitur omnis illa certitudo, quæ jurando quæritur: quæ enim potest esse certitudo illius responsionis, cujus sententia incerta est? Nec expediuntur hac ratione lites, sed augentur magis. Quarto, quia sic jurans proximum suum decipit, & sciens fallit: contra quam exigitur à jurante ne {c}juret in dolo; & contra veterum formulam illam, Si sciens fallo. Quinto, quia ut affirmatio & negatio in assertorio, sic est sponsio in Promissorio juramento, cum contineat in se responsionem ad quæstionem seu interrogationem à deterente propositam, nisi sit congrua & apta propositæ interrogationi, mendacium est & non veritas. Nam ex interrogatione & responsione fit una quasi propositio: quæ omnino falsa censenda est, si alio sensu quam quo proposita est interrogatio, responsio fiat. Neque verò multum adjuvat hac in re istius simulationis patronos restrictio illa quâ uti solent, sc. non licere nobis passim hac æquivocatione uti; Sed solùm apud non-judicem, eum-l. ff. de jurejur.Pf.24 3.

page.notes: The catchword "que" and signature "N 2" are printed at the foot and are not part of the text. The printed "Aft" at the start of the sentence is the long-s form of "Ast" (At) and has been transcribed as "Ast". The marginal reference after "c" reads "Pf.24 3." and the "Pf" is uncertain. The note letters b and c are set in italic in the margin and the reference letters in the text are small. Long s has been rendered as plain s throughout.
